title: Crimson Skies - High Road to Revenge (USA) (En,Fr,De,Zh,Ko).xiso.iso
queue_order: base, then sysmem; each request.sh --title, --device thor, --route crimson-skies, --seconds 240, --perflog, --expect this file
judge: python3 docs/lanes/flip474/phaseread.py --from 120 --to 240 <base> <sysmem>; lockread.py and gfpsseries.py on each over the same window; grep 'env: TU_DEBUG' in each logcat; crashcheck.py and tailcheck.py on each; the shots in the window, by eye
units: GPU, R and X as printed use limits.timestampPeriod; every leg is a ratio of two arms of one binary, or a CPU-clock time, so the period cancels.
prediction: DOA's fight on the Nova (NOTES.md section 16): GMEM executes the draw stream of its one heavy pass twice (X/R 0.99) and sysmem once (X/R 0.02); GPU 34.4 -> 19.6 printed, Tot 64 -> 41 ms, gfps 14 -> 21. X/R from runs on disk: AUF 1.01, Blinx 0.13, Forza 0.25. Crimson paces itself to 30 and reads X/R 0.09 on the Thor (tsperiod.md). lane.turnipfork found the three modes flat at 29 gfps. The capped control: it cannot show a gain, only a cost, and it is the Thor leg (same bundled Turnip).

legs.M0 (instrument): >= 15 hakuX-phase lines with GPU > 0 in the window in each arm, and the shots show play. Otherwise VOID for that arm, rerun once.
legs.E0 (the env reached the app): the sysmem arm's logcat has 'env: TU_DEBUG=sysmem' and the base has no TU_DEBUG line. Otherwise VOID.
legs.T0 (steady): the smallest gfps line in the window is >= 0.6 x the median, unless the shots show a scene change there. Otherwise VOID for that arm (thermal pause, section 15 of NOTES.md).
legs.H0 (no hang): each arm: longest gap between hakuX-perf lines in the window <= 3 s, lines to the end, no crash marker.
legs.C1 (capped, no loss): sysmem's gfps median is within 1 of the base's. Confidence 85%.
legs.C2 (GPU not dearer): sysmem's phase GPU median <= 1.25 x the base's. Confidence 75%. KILL of a global sysmem policy: C1 fails downward with the shots in like scenes.

expect_note: EMPTY ON PURPOSE: a soak writes no captures. The legs are read off hakuX-phase, hakuX-perf and the app's 'env:' lines.
